assumptions: Fixtures and response replays are synthetic; live runs need separately authorized project connections and a named payer.
One provider project, 1..31 complete UTC days plus equal prior window and a bounded 90-day history. At most 200 event types, 2..6 ordered steps, 4 key events, 2 error events and one named dimension.
Run success establishes artifact delivery. Ordinary cases also require a complete useful report and independent numerical/rubric review.
cost_drivers: One bounded Codex session uses the existing pinned model pricing and spending ceiling. No extra managed-model routes. The configured ceiling is not an expected price.

Agent work depends on schema ambiguity, bounded project context, prior state and response/narrative size. Eight provider requests maximum, 16000 bytes each, 64000-byte responses, 900 seconds and one 192000-byte report.
PostHog scans depend on selected window, event volume and actor/attempt cardinality. Output LIMIT is not a bound on provider scan cost. Connected-provider cost is unknown and separate.
Use verified usage from authorized runs for measured estimates. Synthetic SQL checks alone measure no model cost.
effects: Read-only event-definition GET and aggregate query POST through custom.api.posthog. Provider-enforced read-only permissions are required; generic http.write is a transport permission.
One run-owned reports/analytics/<run_id>.md in project state; Files/Activity delivery and existing immutable history.
No provider mutation, raw person exports, credential access, email, publication, workflow activation or recursive runs.

rubric.question: Do ordinary cases contain correct useful figures in all five sections, allowing evidenced absence of pageviews or no supported breakdown, without substituting a diagnostic?
Can every count, rate and timing be reproduced from retained successful aggregates and deterministic calculations, including rejecting plausible inconsistent results?
Are actor identities, attempts, raw emissions, selected-start cohorts, traffic sessions and exclusions labeled correctly, without equating identifiers with humans or inferred setup with value?
Are missing keys, exclusions with missing values, unavailable firing-site semantics and historical coverage explicit, with errors distinguished from zero?
Was one non-identifying dimension chosen before outcomes, with the whole declared family, denominators, Fisher/Holm results and sample/computation limits retained?
Do repeated briefs keep validated labels and meanings, disclose saved-input changes and withhold comparisons on unexplained drift?
Is access limited to the connected project and declared read-only operations, with no sensitive values in the report, recommendations, or unsupported qualification claims?
